title: Staircase net of a cube with faces P to U (3 rows, 4 columns)
bodyMd: The table is the net of a cube drawn on a grid of equal squares, seen from the side on which the letters are printed. Each lettered cell is one square face of the cube; a blank cell is not part of the net. Two faces in cells that share a side are joined along that edge, and the net is folded along those edges to make the cube.

data.caption: Net of a cube seen from its printed side. Lettered cells are faces; blank cells are not part of the net.

accessibilityText: The net of a cube laid out on a grid of three rows and four columns, seen from the printed side, with six lettered square faces arranged like a staircase descending from the top left to the bottom right, and six blank cells that are not part of the net. Row 1: P in Column 1 and Q in Column 2, so P is joined to Q along Q's left edge. Row 2: R in Column 2 and S in Column 3; R is directly below Q and joined to Q along R's top edge, and S is joined to R along R's right edge. Row 3: T in Column 3 and U in Column 4; T is directly below S and joined to S along S's bottom edge, and U is joined to T along T's right edge. All other cells are blank.

provenance.notes: Original net. Face letters run from P to U so that they cannot be confused with the answer labels. A folding script that tracks each face's outward normal (printed side out) confirmed the opposite pairs P and S, Q and T, R and U, and the orientations used by the linked question.
